output.summary: Small coastal tree native broadly to Malesia, Papuasia, eastern Australia and the Pacific, although extensive cultivation makes its exact native island range uncertain. It is braced by aerial roots and bears large segmented fruit resembling a pineapple. The fruit is edible, but some varieties require thorough cooking, while low-oxalate cultivars can be eaten raw.
output.edibilityNote: Fruit and slender seeds are eaten; some varieties require thorough cooking because of calcium oxalate, while low-oxalate cultivars may be eaten raw.
